preconditions.description: Attacker must have some token balance to trigger overflow/underflow
Contract must not be deprecated (deprecated == false) to use vulnerable functions
Contract must not be paused (paused == false)
Attacker must not be blacklisted (isBlackListed[attacker] == false)

violation_target.exploit_hint: Exploit integer overflow/underflow in arithmetic operations without SafeMath. For transfer/transferFrom, use values that cause overflow in fee calculation or balance updates. For issue/redeem functions (if attacker becomes owner), use values that overflow totalSupply or owner balance. The contract uses SafeMath in BasicToken but has unprotected arithmetic in TetherToken's issue() and redeem() functions (using += and -= without SafeMath).

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The TetherToken contract has integer overflow/underflow vulnerabilities in the arithmetic operations of issue() and redeem() functions which use += and -= without SafeMath protection. While require() checks attempt to prevent overflow, in Solidity 0.4.17, integer overflow wraps around. By becoming the owner and manipulating storage to set _totalSupply to near max uint256, we can trigger an overflow that increases the owner's balance dramatically.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Become owner by overwriting the owner storage slot. 2. Ensure contract is not paused or deprecated. 3. Set _totalSupply to max uint256 - 1 via storage manipulation. 4. Call issue(2) which will cause _totalSupply + amount to overflow to 1, passing the require() check (since 1 > max uint256 - 1 is false... wait, actually 1 is NOT > max uint256 - 1, so check fails). Hmm, this won't work. Let me try a different approach: Use the destroyBlackFunds() function which has unprotected subtraction _totalSupply -= dirtyFunds. If we can make dirtyFunds > _totalSupply, this underflows and gives us a huge _totalSupply. Then as owner, we can issue more tokens.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Use vm.store() to become owner (slot 0). 2. Use vm.store() to blacklist ourselves (find isBlackListed mapping slot). 3. Give ourselves a large balance via deal() or storage manipulation. 4. Call destroyBlackFunds() on ourselves. This will set our balance to 0 and cause _totalSupply underflow if our balance > _totalSupply. 5. Now _totalSupply is huge due to underflow. 6. Call issue() to mint tokens for owner (us).
